failure_summary.description: Answers were relevant but mismatched the requested conventional form or scope: number, proper-name components, unnecessary class suffixes, or an overly narrow or expanded title.
The agent missed the requested identity by giving a slogan's description instead of its attribution or by selecting an unrelated neighboring trivia label.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers identifying the requested relation and ignoring unrelated snippets, so the two target-selection failures reflect ignored rules. The form guidance, however, can be clearer: it risks treating conventional name components as disposable while also allowing redundant expansions. Replacing it distinguishes those cases and reinforces matching the answer's scope and number.

edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.
edits.content: Use the conventional answer form that fits the requested slot, preserving supported spelling and grammatical number. Do not drop a word merely because it resembles a category label if it is part of the entity's conventional name. Conversely, when the clue supplies the category and asks for a nickname, brand, or other bare name, do not add a redundant class suffix or expand it to a formal company or adaptation title. Avoid narrowing a general target to a subtype unless the clue or context requires it. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name.
